title: Spectrophotometric Assay of Mitochondrial F1F0 ATP Synthase

Reagents preparation 1- Homogenization buffer (kept at 0-4°C for few weeks or at -20°C for longer period of time)= 225 mM mannitol, 75 mM sucrose, 0.1 mM EDTA, and 10 mM Tris HCl pH 7.2 Anti-protease cocktail at the working concentration given by the manufacturer should be added before use 2- Assay buffer (kept at 0-4°C for few weeks or at -20°C for longer period of time) = 250 mM mannitol, 10 mM KCl, 5 mM MgCl 2, 1 mM EGTA, 1 mg/ml BSA, 50 mM Tris pH 8.25 3- Stock solutions of reagents (kept frozen at -20°C) 0.4 M NADH (diluted in water) 1 mM antimycin A (diluted in dimethylsulfoxide) 250 mM phosphoenopyruvate (diluted in water) 10% w/w dodecylmaltoside (diluted in water) 3 mM P1,P5-Di(adenosine-5')pentaphosphate (AP5A) (diluted in water) 50 mg/mL fatty acid free bovine serumalbumine (diluted in water) 100 mM ATP (diluted in water, adjust pH to 7.5) 1 mM oligomycin (diluted in dimethylsulfoxide) 1 mM IF1 4- Stock solution of enzymes lacticodehydrogenase and pyruvate kinase (kept at 0-4°C)

steps.title: Prepare Assay Medium
steps.instruction: Prepare the required volume of assay medium by adding specific reagents to the assay buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.4 mM NADH (1 µL stock solution per mL of assay buffer); if spectrophotometer response is not linear for at least 2.5 units, use 0.25 mM NADH instead.
Add 1 µM antimycin A (1 µL stock solution per mL of assay buffer).
Add 1 mM PEP (4 µL stock solution per mL of assay buffer).
Add 10 units LDH (volume depending on the batch).
Add 25 units PK (volume depending on the batch).
Add 0.01% w/w DDM (1 µL stock solution per mL of assay buffer).
Add 3 µM AP5A (1 µL stock solution per mL of assay buffer).

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Samples
steps.instruction: Homogenize tissue fragments and isolate the post-nuclear supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Keep muscle, liver, heart, or brain fragments at -80°C until use.
Label one homogenizer and two 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes per sample and keep on ice.
Lightly smash 20 to 50 mg of tissue fragment in a mortar cooled by liquid nitrogen.
Add 9 volumes of homogenization buffer (e.g., 270 µL for a 30 mg fragment).
Manually homogenize on ice (typically 10-20 passes) until the solution is homogeneous, avoiding over-homogenization and heating.
Select pestle based on tissue: use rough glass for muscle and heart; use rough glass or smooth polytetrafluoroethylene for liver and brain.
Transfer homogenate to a pre-cooled 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube and centrifuge at 650 g and 0-4°C for 10 min.
Transfer the supernatant (post-nuclear supernatant) into the second 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Stabilize and Quantify Protein
steps.instruction: Measure protein concentration and stabilize the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Take an aliquot for protein measurement (typical concentration 4 to 7 mg protein/mL; a 1/10 dilution is often used for standards).
Add bovine serum albumin fatty acids-free to a final concentration of 5 mg/mL to stabilize the supernatant for several hours at 0-4°C.

steps.title: Perform Spectrophotometric Assay
steps.instruction: Measure ATP hydrolysis kinetics using a spectrophotometer at 340 nm.

substeps.instruction: Warm 1 mL of assay medium to 37°C in 1 mL spectrophotometric cuvettes (either stirring with a Suprasil TM 109004F-10-40 cuvette or without stirring in a regular plastic cuvette).
Add post-nuclear supernatant (minimum 20 µg protein for brain, 30 µg for heart/muscle, and 40 µg for liver).
If not stirring, seal the cuvette with Parafilm TM and rapidly shake (at least four reversals).
Continuously measure absorbance at 340 nm with a 1 cm optical pathway.
After 3-5 minutes of incubation, trigger the reaction by adding 10 µL of 100 mM ATP (final concentration 1 mM).
After 10-15 minutes, add 5 µL of 1 mM oligomycin (final concentration 5 µM) to measure ATP hydrolysis independent from complex V.
Add 3 µL of 1 mM IF1 (Inhibitory Factor 1) (final concentration 3 µM) to test coupling between F0 and F1 domains.

steps.title: Analyze Kinetic Data
steps.instruction: Calculate the specific complex V ATP hydrolysis activity.

substeps.instruction: Analyze kinetics using εM = 6220 M-1 cm-1.
Subtract the slope obtained after oligomycin addition and after oligomycin + IF1 addition from the slope obtained after ATP addition.
